rules.title: XNA Game Studio build targets import
rules.explanation: The project file imports the XNA Game Studio MSBuild targets (Microsoft.Xna.GameStudio.targets from 3.0 on, Microsoft.Xna.Common.targets and Microsoft.Xna.ContentPipeline.targets in Game Studio Express 1.0). They exist only on machines with the matching XNA Game Studio and Visual Studio installed. Without them the build stops at once with MSB4019 (imported project not found), as it did for Pirate-Treasure-Hunter.
rules.resolution: The migrator writes an SDK-style project for .NET 8 that does not import the XNA targets.

rules.title: XNA-specific project properties
rules.explanation: The project sets XnaFrameworkVersion, a property that only the XNA Game Studio targets understand. The same project usually also sets ProjectTypeGuids (the XNA game GUID), XnaPlatform, XnaProfile, XnaOutputType, XnaCrossPlatformGroupID, and in Game Studio Express 1.0 XNAGlobalContentPipelineAssemblies and XNAProjectContentPipelineAssemblies. None has an MSBuild equivalent in MonoGame.
rules.resolution: The migrator drops XNA-specific properties and project type GUIDs when it generates the SDK-style project. The graphics profile is carried into Content.mgcb as /profile.

rules.title: XNA assembly references
rules.explanation: The project references XNA assemblies (Microsoft.Xna.Framework and related) by strong name with Private=False. They do not resolve on a machine without XNA, so the project cannot build. MonoGame ships the same API under the same namespaces in its own package. This rule also fires for assemblies MonoGame does not provide (GamerServices, Net, Avatar, Storage, Xact, Video); those have their own rules for code that uses them.
rules.resolution: The migrator replaces the XNA references with the MonoGame DesktopGL or WindowsDX package.

rules.title: Old .NET Framework target
rules.explanation: The project targets the .NET Framework (3.5 for XNA 3.x, 4.0 with the Client profile for XNA 4.0). That framework version is not available to an SDK-style build, and current MonoGame releases need modern .NET.
rules.resolution: The migrator sets the target framework of the generated project to net8.0.

rules.title: Nested XNA content project
rules.explanation: Assets live in a nested .contentproj that imports the XNA content pipeline targets, which only XNA Game Studio can build. MonoGame builds content from a Content.mgcb file. Projects that reference the content project with a ProjectReference instead are covered by XNA049.
rules.resolution: The migrator generates Content.mgcb from the content project, copies the source assets, and lists anything it cannot convert as manual work.

rules.title: XNA 3.x project
rules.explanation: The project targets XNA 3.0 or 3.1. XNA 4.0 broke much of the graphics, storage, and effect API, and MonoGame follows the 4.0 API. Premultiplied alpha is also the default from 4.0 on, so sprite blending can look different after the move. Each concrete break has its own rule.
rules.resolution: Fix the findings from the XNA 3.x rules, then compare the rendered result of the migrated game with the original, especially alpha-blended sprites.

rules.title: Project targets Xbox 360, Zune, or Windows Phone
rules.explanation: XnaPlatform names a device platform (Xbox 360, Zune, or Windows Phone). The project cannot run on a desktop as it is, because it depends on device APIs and device-only #if branches. The device rules XNA053 to XNA063 list what the code uses.
rules.resolution: The migrator turns the project into a Windows DesktopGL game: it skips platform copies of the same game, folds the device #if branches, and adds stand-ins that map touch, tilt, and the Back button to the mouse and keyboard. What it cannot convert is listed as manual work.

rules.title: Content pipeline extension assembly reference
rules.explanation: The project references the XNA content pipeline base assembly, so it is a custom importer, processor, or content type library. The XNA pipeline types cannot run in the MonoGame content builder.
rules.resolution: Recreate the library against the MonoGame content pipeline package, then reference it from Content.mgcb with /reference.

rules.title: GamerServices (Xbox Live, Guide, gamer profiles)
rules.explanation: Code uses GamerServices (Guide, SignedInGamer, achievements, leaderboards, trial mode). MonoGame removed this namespace and no replacement exists for the Xbox Live services behind it.
rules.resolution: Remove the calls or replace them with your own sign-in, saving, and leaderboard code. Remove GamerServicesComponent from the Game constructor.

rules.title: Net (NetworkSession, system link, Live multiplayer)
rules.explanation: Code uses the XNA Net namespace (NetworkSession, PacketReader, PacketWriter). MonoGame removed it, and it depended on Xbox Live matchmaking.
rules.resolution: Rewrite networking with System.Net.Sockets or a library such as Lidgren.Network.

rules.title: Avatar API (Xbox 360 avatars)
rules.explanation: Code uses the XNA Avatar API (AvatarRenderer, AvatarDescription, AvatarAnimation). It only worked on Xbox 360 with Xbox Live and MonoGame has no equivalent.
rules.resolution: Replace avatars with your own character models and remove the Avatar code.

rules.title: Storage (StorageDevice, StorageContainer)
rules.explanation: Code uses StorageDevice and StorageContainer for save games. MonoGame removed the Storage namespace because it did not port across platforms.
rules.resolution: Write saves with System.IO under Environment.SpecialFolder.ApplicationData and read packaged files with TitleContainer.OpenStream. The optional shim project (project-migrator:12.1) can stand in for the calls while you rewrite.

rules.title: XNA-only SpriteFont family
rules.explanation: A .spritefont names a font from the XNA Redistributable Font Pack, which XNA Game Studio 4.0 installed and Windows does not ship (Andy, Jing Jing, Kootenay, Lindsey, Miramonte, Moire, Motorwerk, News Gothic, Pericles, Pescadero, Quartz MS, Segoe Keycaps, Segoe UI Mono, Wasco Sans). The MonoGame content builder looks the font up in the system font folders, so the content build fails with 'Could not find ... font file' for each such file (Pirate-Treasure-Hunter: Pescadero in three files, Segoe UI Mono in one). The list matches src/XnaReborn.Migrator/Content/data/xna-only-fonts.json.
rules.resolution: Change FontName to an installed or bundled font, or add a .ttf to the content folder and name it. The migrator can substitute a close Windows font in the migrated copy when font substitution is turned on. Glyph widths differ from the original, so check the layout.

rules.title: Video playback (VideoPlayer, Video)
rules.explanation: Code plays video with VideoPlayer. MonoGame has the class, but video support depends on the platform. The DesktopGL target has historically lacked working video playback and the WMV importer is Windows only.
rules.resolution: Test playback on the chosen target. If it fails, convert the video and use a video library such as a Theora or FFmpeg player.

rules.title: XACT audio engine (AudioEngine, WaveBank, SoundBank, Cue)
rules.explanation: Code uses the XACT runtime. MonoGame can load compiled XACT files (.xgs, .xwb, .xsb) but the content builder cannot compile XACT projects, and some features such as ADPCM and streaming wave banks are limited.
rules.resolution: Ship the compiled XACT files unchanged and load them by path, or move sounds to SoundEffect and Song assets and drop XACT.

rules.title: XACT project file (.xap)
rules.explanation: The project contains an XACT authoring file. XACT is a Windows-only tool that is no longer updated, and the MonoGame content builder does not compile .xap files.
rules.resolution: Compile the project in XACT and copy the .xgs, .xwb, and .xsb outputs, or export the sounds as wav or ogg files and use SoundEffect and Song.

rules.title: Effect file (.fx) needs shader review
rules.explanation: XNA compiled .fx files with the legacy DirectX 9 compiler. MonoGame uses a different compiler and imposes restrictions, so old shaders can fail to build or render differently. The migrator fixes shader models and two sampler state names, marks the constructs it cannot fix, and copies included files; a person still has to check the look.
rules.resolution: Read the notes and marker comments the migrator left in the copied effect, build it with the MonoGame content builder, fix compile errors, and compare the output. The MonoGame custom effects guide lists the limits.

rules.title: Prebuilt .xnb files
rules.explanation: The project folder holds compiled .xnb assets. They cannot be rebuilt for MonoGame without the source files, and an .xnb built for another platform or XNA version may fail to load.
rules.resolution: Find the original source assets and add them to the content project. If none exist, test loading each .xnb in the migrated game.

rules.title: WMA audio
rules.explanation: WMA audio is an old Windows format. MonoGame imports it but advises against it for cross-platform games.
rules.resolution: The migrator maps WMA to the MonoGame WMA importer and Song processor. Convert to ogg or mp3 later if the game must run beyond Windows.

rules.title: WMV video content
rules.explanation: The content project builds a WMV video. MonoGame's WMV importer only works on Windows and video playback is not available on every target.
rules.resolution: Test the content build on the chosen target. Re-encode the video or use a video playback library if it fails.

rules.title: Skinned model processor from the XNA sample
rules.explanation: A model uses SkinnedModelProcessor, a custom processor from the XNA skinned model sample. It lives in a pipeline library built against XNA and has to be rebuilt for MonoGame.
rules.resolution: Port the SkinnedModel pipeline and runtime libraries to MonoGame packages and reference the pipeline library from Content.mgcb.

rules.title: SpriteBlendMode (replaced by BlendState)
rules.explanation: SpriteBlendMode and the SpriteBatch.Begin overloads that take it were removed in XNA 4.0 and are not in MonoGame. Uses outside a Begin call cannot be rewritten safely.
rules.resolution: The migrator rewrites Begin(SpriteBlendMode.X) to Begin(SpriteSortMode.Deferred, BlendState.X) and marks other uses for manual work.

rules.title: SaveStateMode (removed)
rules.explanation: SaveStateMode, used in SpriteBatch.Begin and Effect.Begin, was removed in XNA 4.0 together with StateBlock. Graphics state is no longer saved and restored for you.
rules.resolution: Delete the argument and set the blend, depth, rasterizer, and sampler state explicitly before each draw.

rules.title: GraphicsDevice.RenderState (replaced by state objects)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 replaced RenderState with BlendState, DepthStencilState, and RasterizerState. A user type with a member named RenderState would also match.
rules.resolution: The migrator replaces known RenderState assignments with state objects and marks combinations it cannot map with confidence.

rules.title: StateBlock (removed)
rules.explanation: StateBlock saved and restored device state. It was removed in XNA 4.0 because it was very slow.
rules.resolution: Set every state you depend on before drawing, or keep the previous state objects in local variables and assign them back.

rules.title: SamplerState MinFilter, MagFilter, MipFilter (merged into Filter)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 merged the three filter properties of a sampler into one Filter property and made sampler states immutable objects. The rule detects MagFilter only; code that sets MinFilter or MipFilter alone is missed.
rules.resolution: Pick a built-in SamplerState such as LinearClamp or PointWrap, or create a SamplerState with the Filter you need and assign it to GraphicsDevice.SamplerStates[n].

rules.title: ResolveTexture2D (removed)
rules.explanation: ResolveTexture2D copied the back buffer into a texture. XNA 4.0 removed it, and MonoGame has no back buffer resolve.
rules.resolution: Draw the scene into a RenderTarget2D and use that render target as a texture.

rules.title: GraphicsDevice.ResolveBackBuffer (removed)
rules.explanation: ResolveBackBuffer was removed in XNA 4.0. Any method with the same name in a game class would also match.
rules.resolution: Call SetRenderTarget with a RenderTarget2D before drawing the scene, then SetRenderTarget(null) and draw the render target.

rules.title: DepthStencilBuffer (removed)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 removed DepthStencilBuffer and GraphicsDevice.DepthStencilBuffer. The depth format is now part of each render target.
rules.resolution: Pass a DepthFormat to the RenderTarget2D constructor and delete the code that creates, sets, and restores depth buffers.

rules.title: RenderTarget2D.GetTexture (removed)
rules.explanation: RenderTarget2D now derives from Texture2D, so GetTexture was removed. Parameterless GetTexture methods on other types also match.
rules.resolution: Use the render target itself wherever a Texture2D is expected. Create a new render target per saved frame instead of reusing one.

rules.title: SetRenderTarget(index, target)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 sets all render targets in one call and has no index argument. The two-argument form still exists for cube map targets, so a valid call such as SetRenderTarget(cube, CubeMapFace.PositiveX) also matches.
rules.resolution: Use SetRenderTarget(target) for one target, SetRenderTarget(null) to return to the back buffer, and SetRenderTargets(a, b, c) for several.

rules.title: PresentationParameters.MultiSampleType (replaced by MultiSampleCount)
rules.explanation: PresentationParameters.MultiSampleType and MultiSampleQuality were replaced by an integer MultiSampleCount in XNA 4.0. Render targets take the count in their constructor.
rules.resolution: Use MultiSampleCount (0 for none, 4 for 4x) and remove MultiSampleQuality.

rules.title: PresentationParameters.AutoDepthStencilFormat (replaced by DepthStencilFormat)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 removed EnableAutoDepthStencil and AutoDepthStencilFormat. PresentationParameters now has DepthStencilFormat, and DepthFormat.None disables the depth buffer.
rules.resolution: Set DepthStencilFormat, or GraphicsDeviceManager.PreferredDepthStencilFormat, and delete EnableAutoDepthStencil.

rules.title: GraphicsDevice.VertexDeclaration (removed)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 removed the device property because every vertex buffer now carries its declaration. Known limit: the receiver must be named GraphicsDevice, so code that uses another variable name is missed. The name is needed to avoid the valid static VertexDeclaration property of the 4.0 vertex types.
rules.resolution: Delete the assignment and create the VertexBuffer with a vertex type or a VertexDeclaration.

rules.title: GraphicsDevice.Vertices[n].SetSource (replaced by SetVertexBuffer)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 removed GraphicsDevice.Vertices. Vertex buffers are set with SetVertexBuffer, and buffer sizes are counted in vertices instead of bytes.
rules.resolution: Replace the call with GraphicsDevice.SetVertexBuffer(buffer). Use SetVertexBuffers for several streams. Change buffer sizes from bytes to vertex counts.

rules.title: VertexElements on vertex types (removed)
rules.explanation: XNA 3.x vertex structs exposed a VertexElements array. In 4.0 they expose a VertexDeclaration, and the VertexDeclaration constructor no longer takes a GraphicsDevice.
rules.resolution: Use VertexPositionColor.VertexDeclaration, or new VertexDeclaration(new VertexElement(...)) for custom vertex types, and implement IVertexType on custom structs.

rules.title: ModelMeshPart.VertexStride (removed)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 moved the vertex and index buffers from ModelMesh to ModelMeshPart and removed VertexStride, StreamOffset, and VertexDeclaration from the part. Custom model drawing code breaks.
rules.resolution: Set meshPart.VertexBuffer and meshPart.IndexBuffer on the device and read the layout from VertexBuffer.VertexDeclaration.

rules.title: BufferUsage.Points and point sprites (removed)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 dropped point sprites. The point-size render states are gone with them, and MonoGame has no BufferUsage.Points. Known limit: the receiver is matched by the name BufferUsage, so an alias or a using static import is missed.
rules.resolution: Draw each point as a textured quad, or draw billboards with SpriteBatch or an instanced quad.

rules.title: EffectPass.Begin and End (replaced by Apply)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 replaced EffectPass.Begin and End with EffectPass.Apply. Known limit: the rule only sees calls on a variable named pass, which is the usual loop variable, so passes held in variables with other names are missed.
rules.resolution: The migrator rewrites the Begin/End pattern to pass.Apply() and marks patterns it cannot rewrite with confidence.

rules.title: Effect.Begin and End (replaced by EffectPass.Apply)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 removed Effect.Begin and End. Known limit: the rule only sees calls on a variable named effect, so effects held in other variables (basicEffect, shader, and so on) are missed.
rules.resolution: The migrator replaces the Begin/End pattern with a loop over CurrentTechnique.Passes that calls Apply, and marks patterns it cannot rewrite with confidence.

rules.title: Effect.CommitChanges (removed)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 removed Effect.CommitChanges. Parameter values are sent to the device when EffectPass.Apply runs.
rules.resolution: Delete the call and make sure EffectPass.Apply runs after the last parameter change and before the draw call.

rules.title: GameTime.TotalRealTime and ElapsedRealTime (removed)
rules.explanation: XNA 4.0 removed the real-time members of GameTime. Only game time remains. The rule detects TotalRealTime; ElapsedRealTime is missed.
rules.resolution: Use TotalGameTime and ElapsedGameTime. If wall-clock time is needed, use a Stopwatch.

rules.title: ShaderProfile (removed)
rules.explanation: GraphicsDeviceManager.MinimumPixelShaderProfile and MinimumVertexShaderProfile were replaced in XNA 4.0 by GraphicsProfile (Reach or HiDef). MonoGame has no ShaderProfile.
rules.resolution: Delete the shader profile settings. Set GraphicsProfile to Reach or HiDef if the game needs to choose.

rules.title: ClickOnce bootstrapper packages
rules.explanation: The project lists ClickOnce bootstrapper packages, which come from the Publish tab of Visual Studio 2010 (the XNA templates include the XNA Framework redistributable). The same settings usually bring a hard-coded PublishUrl, ManifestKeyFile, and manifest signing. Nothing in an SDK-style MonoGame build uses them. Known limit: only BootstrapperPackage items trigger the rule, not the publish properties alone.
rules.resolution: The migrator writes a new SDK-style project that carries none of the publish settings. Publish the MonoGame game with dotnet publish.

rules.title: Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs duplicates SDK attributes
rules.explanation: Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs declares assembly attributes (title, product, company, version). An SDK-style project generates the same attributes from project properties, and the build then fails with CS0579 duplicate attribute. Pirate-Treasure-Hunter got four errors from this one file.
rules.resolution: The migrator writes <GenerateAssemblyInfo>false</GenerateAssemblyInfo> in the generated project so the kept AssemblyInfo.cs does not clash.

rules.title: NoStdLib breaks SDK-style builds
rules.explanation: NoStdLib=true tells the compiler not to reference the standard library. The old XNA project templates set it. An SDK-style project supplies the references itself, so the compiler would miss System.Object and the build would fail.
rules.resolution: The migrator writes a new SDK-style project from a fixed property set that does not include NoStdLib.

rules.title: Signing key (.pfx) in the project folder
rules.explanation: A .pfx file sits in the project folder. XNA templates create a temporary key for ClickOnce manifest signing. A private key committed to source control is a leak risk, and nothing in a MonoGame build uses it.
rules.resolution: Do not carry the file into the new project. If the key was ever used for real signing, treat it as exposed and replace it, and remove it from the repository history if the repository is public.

rules.title: Content project referenced with ProjectReference
rules.explanation: The game project references a .contentproj with a ProjectReference (XnaReferenceType Content), the form used when the content project is a sibling project. MonoGame cannot load that reference and builds content from Content.mgcb instead. The analyzer reads this content project like a nested one, so the content-item rules (XNA017, XNA019, XNA020, XNA021) see the assets behind this form.
rules.resolution: The migrator removes the reference, generates Content.mgcb from the content project like it does for a nested content project (XNA005), copies the source assets into the game project, and lists anything it cannot convert as manual work.

rules.title: Custom content importer or processor
rules.explanation: A content item uses an importer or processor that is not part of stock XNA 4.0. It comes from a custom content pipeline assembly, which was built against the XNA pipeline and does not load in the MonoGame content builder as it is.
rules.resolution: Port the pipeline project to MonoGame and reference the rebuilt assembly from Content.mgcb, or replace the asset with one that a stock importer and processor can build.

rules.title: Windows Phone Silverlight application
rules.explanation: The project is a Silverlight application (SilverlightApplication is true). Its pages, XAML and navigation have no MonoGame equivalent. This rule is provisional: the property set was written from the Microsoft documentation, not checked against a real hybrid project.
rules.resolution: Move the XNA game code into a plain XNA project first, then migrate that project. The Silverlight pages have to be rebuilt by hand.

rules.title: Platform copy of another project
rules.explanation: At least half of this project's Compile items are links to files of another project. Game Studio's Create Copy of project for a platform command makes projects like this: they share the code of the original and add nothing of their own.
rules.resolution: The migrator migrates one project of the group (the Windows one when there is one) and skips each copy. You can change the choice in the migration plan.

rules.title: Device conditional compilation symbols
rules.explanation: An #if or #elif directive names a platform symbol (XBOX, XBOX360, ZUNE, WINDOWS_PHONE, or WINDOWS). The migrated project defines none of them, so the wrong branch would be compiled. Inactive branches count too.
rules.resolution: The migrator keeps the branch that is true for the chosen platform and removes the other branches. A condition that also depends on another symbol, such as DEBUG, is left as it is with a marker.

rules.title: Marketplace trial mode
rules.explanation: Code reads Guide.IsTrialMode. Trial mode and the marketplace belong to the Xbox and Phone stores, which no longer exist.
rules.resolution: The migrator adds a stand-in Guide member that always reports a full version.

rules.title: Marketplace launchers and license types
rules.explanation: Code uses a Windows Phone marketplace launcher or LicenseInformation. The Windows Phone marketplace is gone.
rules.resolution: The migrator adds stand-in types that do nothing, and LicenseInformation reports a full version.

rules.title: Zune media library
rules.explanation: Code browses the device media library (songs, albums, playlists). MonoGame has no media library.
rules.resolution: Replace the library calls with your own list of files, or remove the feature.

rules.title: Phone application service (tombstoning)
rules.explanation: Code uses PhoneApplicationService to keep state when the phone deactivates the game.
rules.resolution: The migrator adds a stand-in with an in-memory State dictionary. Its events never fire.

rules.title: Phone launchers
rules.explanation: Code starts a phone launcher task (browser, e-mail, call, SMS, or marketplace hub).
rules.resolution: The migrator adds stand-ins whose Show() writes one log line and does nothing else.

rules.title: Phone choosers
rules.explanation: Code uses a phone chooser task (photo, camera, or ringtone). Choosers return a result through a Completed event that never fires on a desktop.
rules.resolution: Replace the chooser with a file dialog or remove the feature.

rules.title: Accelerometer
rules.explanation: Code reads the phone accelerometer. A desktop has none, and MonoGame's Accelerometer is a stub in another namespace.
rules.resolution: The migrator adds an Accelerometer with the same members that is driven by the keyboard (arrow keys or W, A, S, D).

rules.title: TouchPanel and gestures
rules.explanation: Code reads touch input. MonoGame has TouchPanel, but on a desktop it only reports the mouse after two switches are turned on.
rules.resolution: The migrator adds a game component that turns the mouse touch point and mouse gestures on at startup.

rules.title: GamePad.GetState (keyboard fallback and Back button)
rules.explanation: Code reads the game pad. A phone or Zune has no pad, only a Back button, and many desktops have no pad either. The check is by name only: a game class called GamePad in another namespace is not told apart from the XNA one.
rules.resolution: The migrator changes the call to a replacement that returns the real pad when one is connected, and keyboard input otherwise (Escape is Back).

rules.title: Third-party device assembly
rules.explanation: The project references an advertising assembly made for Windows Phone. It has no desktop version.
rules.resolution: Remove the reference and the code that uses it, or replace it with a desktop service.

rules.title: XNA 1.0 or 2.0 project
rules.explanation: The project targets XNA Game Studio Express 1.0 or XNA Game Studio 2.0. Both are older than the 3.x line. Everything in XNA 4.0 and MonoGame that changed since 3.1 changed since these versions too. Defaults also differ: premultiplied alpha is the default from 4.0 on, and from 2.0 on Draw is called once per Update with a fixed time step, so a frame counter that counted Draw calls reads differently. Visual Basic projects are covered by a separate group of rules.
rules.resolution: Fix the findings from the XNA 1.0 and 2.0 rules and the XNA 3.x rules, then compare the rendered result of the migrated game with the original, especially alpha-blended sprites and anything that depends on frame timing.

rules.title: Content built inside the game project
rules.explanation: XNA Game Studio Express 1.0 lists content files as Content items inside the game project (marked XNAUseContentPipeline), with the importer and processor on each item. Later versions use a separate content project. MonoGame builds content from a Content.mgcb file.
rules.resolution: The migrator reads these items like a content project and writes a Content.mgcb file for them.

rules.title: LoadGraphicsContent (replaced by LoadContent)
rules.explanation: XNA 1.0 called LoadGraphicsContent(bool loadAllContent) when the graphics device was created or reset. XNA 2.0 replaced it by LoadContent(), which runs once. The override does not exist in MonoGame, so the game does not compile. The check is by name and the override modifier only.
rules.resolution: The migrator renames the override to LoadContent, drops the parameter and adds a constant with the old parameter name set to true, so the body keeps compiling. Calls by name and unusual signatures are marked for manual work.

rules.title: UnloadGraphicsContent (replaced by UnloadContent)
rules.explanation: XNA 1.0 called UnloadGraphicsContent(bool unloadAllContent) when the graphics device was lost. XNA 2.0 replaced it by UnloadContent(). The override does not exist in MonoGame. The check is by name and the override modifier only.
rules.resolution: The migrator renames the override to UnloadContent, drops the parameter and adds a constant with the old parameter name set to true. Calls by name and unusual signatures are marked for manual work.

rules.title: ResourceManagementMode (removed)
rules.explanation: XNA 1.0 let a game choose whether the framework or the game reloaded textures and vertex buffers after a device reset. The device was virtualized in 2.0, so the type is gone and MonoGame does not have it. Constructor overloads that take it fail to compile.
rules.resolution: Use the overload without a ResourceManagementMode and load the resources in LoadContent.

rules.title: ResourceUsage (removed)
rules.explanation: XNA 1.0 resource constructors took a ResourceUsage value. It was removed together with the resource management modes, and MonoGame does not have it. Which exact version dropped it was not confirmed, so the rule runs on 1.0 and 2.0.
rules.resolution: Use the overload without a ResourceUsage argument. Pass BufferUsage where the new overload asks for it.

rules.title: Fixed shader model in an effect
rules.explanation: A compile statement names a Shader Model 1 to 3 profile. The DirectX compiler in MonoGame only accepts Shader Model 4 level 9 or higher, so the effect fails to build for WindowsDX. A macro that sets the model in a template-style #define is not found by this rule.
rules.resolution: The migrator replaces the models with macros that pick the original on OpenGL and a Shader Model 4 level 9 profile on DirectX. Check the rendered result.

rules.title: Effect pass state MonoGame does not support
rules.explanation: A pass sets a render state that the MonoGame effect compiler does not accept, such as alpha testing. The effect fails to build. This rule looks for the common old state names; the migrator checks every pass against the full list of accepted states.
rules.resolution: Set the state in C# (for example AlphaTestEffect for alpha testing) or discard in the pixel shader. The migrator adds a marker comment above each line.

rules.title: Effect syntax MonoGame does not parse
rules.explanation: The effect uses an annotation, arguments in a compile statement, or Direct3D 10 shader calls. The MonoGame effect parser does not accept them and the effect fails to build.
rules.resolution: Remove the annotation, move the arguments into the shader function, or use VertexShader = compile and PixelShader = compile. The migrator adds a marker comment above each line.

rules.title: Effect uses VPOS
rules.explanation: A pixel shader reads its screen position from VPOS. The MonoGame effect compiler does not support that input on either target.
rules.resolution: Use SV_Position as the pixel shader input on DirectX, and compute the screen position from the vertex shader output on OpenGL. The migrator adds a marker comment.

rules.title: Old sampler state name or filter
rules.explanation: A sampler uses MipMapLodBias, or the GaussianQuad or PyramidalQuad filter. MonoGame calls the first MipLodBias and has neither filter.
rules.resolution: The migrator renames MipMapLodBias to MipLodBias and replaces the two filters with Linear. Check the look.

rules.title: Effect parameter with a default value
rules.explanation: A top-level effect parameter has a default value. OpenGL targets ignore it, and the compiler removes parameters that the shader never uses.
rules.resolution: Set the value from code. The migration report lists defaults and unused parameters per file.
